Zakaria  · Updated 4 days ago\n\narrow\\_drop\\_up0\n\ncodeCode\n\nfile\\_downloadDownload\n\nmore\\_vert\n\n# RSNA Knee: LLM report labels and folds\n\nSoft labels from radiology reports, 5-fold split and training script\n\n![](https://storage.googleapis.com/kaggle-datasets-images/new-version-temp-images/default-backgrounds-38.png-4495635/dataset-cover.png)\n\n## RSNA Knee: LLM report labels and folds\n\n[Data Card](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/nartaa/rsna-knee-hpo-assets/data) [Code (0)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/nartaa/rsna-knee-hpo-assets/code) [Discussion (0)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/nartaa/rsna-knee-hpo-assets/discussion) [Suggestions (0)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/nartaa/rsna-knee-hpo-assets/suggestions)\n\n## About Dataset\n\nTraining assets for the [RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rsna-knee-abnormality-detection) competition: four sets of soft training labels, the report-derived truths used to score them, a fixed 5-fold split and the training script they were used with.\n\n## Why labels\n\nThe competition has 4,407 training studies. Structured labels exist for only 58 of them (the \"gold\" studies); the other 4,349 come with a free-text radiology report. Before a model can train, each report has to become twelve numbers, one per finding.\n\n## The label files\n\nAll four have one row per non-gold training study (4,349 rows), a `StudyInstanceUID` column and the twelve finding columns, each a soft probability in \\[0, 1\\].\n\n- **labels\\_v0raw.parquet**: the public v4\\_blend report labels from [stevenleehans/rsna-knee-llm-report-labels](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/stevenleehans/rsna-knee-llm-report-labels), unchanged. A cell of exactly 0.25 means the report did not address that finding.\n- **labels\\_v1\\_gemlow.parquet**: every report re-read by gemini-3-flash (reasoning effort low) against the host's image-annotation definitions for the twelve findings. For each finding the model returns present, absent or not addressed, a calibrated probability and a quote from the report. Silent findings keep the model's prior probability.\n- **labels\\_v1\\_blend.parquet**: the mean of gemlow and v4\\_blend wherever v4\\_blend addressed the finding; gemlow alone where v4\\_blend holds its 0.25 marker.\n- **labels\\_v1\\_perlabel.parquet**: a per-finding pick among the three sets above, chosen on the 58 gold studies. It did not beat the blend in training (per-finding AUC on 58 studies is mostly noise), and is kept for completeness.\n\n## Scoring truths\n\n- **train\\_labels\\_v0.parquet** (4,407 rows): `y_{finding}` = v4\\_blend value, `m_{finding}` = 1 if the report addressed the finding, `is_gold`, and `gold_{finding}` = the structured label for the 58 gold studies.\n- **train\\_labels\\_v1.parquet** (4,407 rows): `y_{finding}` = gemini probability, `m_{finding}` = 1 if the report addressed the finding.\n\nA model trained on one label set always scores best on its own report truth, so these truths can't choose between label sets. Use the gold studies or the leaderboard for that.\n\n## Split and code\n\n- **folds\\_v0.json**: `{\"folds\": {StudyInstanceUID: fold}}`. Folds 0–4 hold 869–870 studies each; the 58 gold studies are fold −1 and never train.\n- **train\\_knee.py**: the training script these labels were used with, adapted from dreaddevelopment's [Knee MRI: training the twelve-finding model](https://www.kaggle.com/code/dreaddevelopment/knee-mri-training-the-twelve-finding-model). It uses a timm backbone (CoAtNet or ResNet) with a per-finding attention-pooling head over three-slice windows. It reads the preprocessed corpus from [knee-raptor-corpus](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dreaddevelopment/knee-raptor-corpus) and [knee-raptor-corpus-ext](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dreaddevelopment/knee-raptor-corpus-ext). Its flags cover fold training, all-data training, a time budget with resume, fp16 or bf16 and TPU (XLA).\n- **hpo\\_worker.py**: a remote Optuna worker for a hyper-parameter screen. It needs your own server address and token in environment variables; none are included.\n- **xla\\_probe.py**: a timing probe for training on a Kaggle TPU.\n\n## One measured result\n\nOn fold 0 (870 held-out studies) with the same CoAtNet recipe, the epoch-ensemble score on the 58 gold studies was 0.888 with labels\\_v0raw, 0.904 with labels\\_v1\\_gemlow and 0.904 with labels\\_v1\\_blend. With 58 studies the noise is about ±0.03.\n\nexpand\\_moreView more\n\n## Usability\n\ninfo\n\n7.06\n\n## License\n\n[CC0: Public Domain](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)\n\n## Expected update frequency\n\nNever\n\n## Tags\n\n[Image](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets?tags=14102-Image) [Classification](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets?tags=13302-Classification) [Health](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets?tags=11111-Health) [NLP](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets?tags=13204-NLP) [Deep Learning](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets?tags=13310-Deep+Learning) [Healthcare](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets?tags=4202-Healthcare) [Medicine](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets?tags=12028-Medicine)\n\n## folds\\_v0.json(312.97 kB)\n\nget\\_app\n\nfullscreen\n\nchevron\\_right\n\nerror\n\nThis preview is truncated due to the large file size.
